title: Backend Quality Suite — project profile
description: Schema for .backend-suite/profile.json. The suite's engines carry no project literals; everything project-specific is declared here. `backend-suite doctor` validates a profile against this schema and additionally checks that every declared path resolves.

relativePath.description: A repo-relative path. Absolute paths, home-relative paths, Windows drive paths, and parent-escapes are all rejected: a committed absolute path is machine-specific and silently inert on every other checkout. This repo has a live instance of that bug in .claude/settings.json (four dead /Users/<name>/... entries), which is why the prohibition is in the schema rather than a convention.

provenanceEntry.description: How one profile field got its value. RFC-0002 §3b: inference without provenance is indistinguishable from a fact, so a machine's guess must never be able to wear a human decision's clothes.

state.description: 'inferred' — a survey or a skill proposed it, and nothing downstream may treat it as authoritative. 'declared' — a human wrote it. 'approved' — a human reviewed an inferred value and ratified it. There is deliberately no fourth value here: 'contradicted' is COMPUTED by doctor.py when an approved or declared field stops matching the tree, and storing it would make a stale fact re-assertable by hand (RFC-0002 §3h).

by.description: Who decided it. Required in spirit for 'declared'/'approved' — an unattributed ratification cannot be re-examined — but not schema-required, because refusing to record provenance at all is worse than recording it anonymously.

on.description: ISO date of the decision. Informational only: staleness is measured in diffs via verifiedAgainst.commit, never in days (RFC-0002 §3h rejects a calendar TTL on approvals outright).

value.description: The field's value as ratified. doctor.py compares it against the profile's live value: a difference means the value was edited after ratification and the ratification no longer covers it. Optional — omitting it only narrows what can be contradicted.

evidence.description: Why this state is justified — the survey signal, or the reasoning a skill argued from. Load-bearing for 'inferred', since ratifying a proposal means reviewing its argument.

verifiedAgainst.description: The tree this field was last confirmed against. RFC-0002 §3h's `verified_against`, spelled camelCase for consistency with the rest of this file. A timestamp makes staleness a calendar guess; a commit makes it a diff — 'verified against a tree 339 commits ago' is a fact, 'verified 24 days ago' is an eyebrow-raise.

commit.description: Full or abbreviated git SHA of the tree the value was confirmed against.

dirty.description: True when the working tree differed from that commit at confirmation time. A confirmation against uncommitted work that reads as a confirmation of HEAD is a lie, so it is stamped rather than forbidden.

audience.description: Who uses the product. Feeds copy and accessibility judgement.

framework.description: Free text, read by prompts. Include deliberate non-features (e.g. 'light-only') so audits do not report them as gaps.

singleLocale.description: Set when the project is deliberately single-locale, so no skill proposes i18n scaffolding.

projectKind.description: Which archetype this repository is. Selects which doc roles are expected, which discovery runs, and which audits apply at all. The enum is closed on purpose: a value outside it is a refusal, never a fall-through to 'app' — assuming 'app' for a package is what makes a scaffolder emit an empty flows document and an audit report clean on documents it never looked for. Optional, so an existing profile keeps working; anything that needs the kind must then say it does not know rather than assume one. Vocabulary mirrored in templates/docs/roles.json, which also carries per-role applicability.

workspace.description: True when this repository is a container of archetypes (a monorepo). Deliberately an orthogonal flag rather than a fourth projectKind: as a kind it would force a repo holding an app and a package to pick one and be wrong either way. Each role in roles.json declares whether it resolves once at workspace root or once per member.

adapters.description: Which implementation fills each stack seam. Unknown values fail fast rather than silently no-op.

source._rootsComment: `root` was required outright until multi-root support landed (RFC-0002 §3g #3). It is now one of two accepted ways to say the same thing, so every existing profile — both live consumers declare only `root` — validates unchanged. What is NOT accepted is declaring neither: a profile with no source tree at all would make every source audit sweep nothing and report clean.

roots.description: Every source tree this project has, for a workspace whose top-level manifest is a stub and whose real sources live in its members. Optional and additive: when absent, `root` answers as it always did; when present, it wins and `root` is ignored. Sweeps union these roots; findings stay repo-relative, so the path itself names the root it came from and no second identifier can drift from it. Declaring neither key is a refusal, not a fallback to the repository root.

routesFile.description: Project-relative path to the file that DECLARES route paths. Read by /review-docs check C. Not necessarily the file that builds the router.

debt.description: Configuration for /quality-debt. `audits` is what makes a never-run audit visible: the dashboard reads .backend-suite/findings/, and an audit that has never run leaves no file there, so inferring the expected set from what exists on disk would render its absence invisible.

audits.description: Audits this project expects to have collected findings for, named by the audit key that matches the envelope's `audit` field.

thresholds.description: Per-audit, per-category grade bands overriding the engine defaults. 144 findings in a 382-file tree and 144 in a 40-file one are not the same condition, and the engine cannot tell which it is looking at.

violationBands.description: [[maxCount, grade], ...] ascending. First band whose count is not exceeded wins; past the last is F.

passRateBands.description: [[minRate, grade], ...] descending, for audits that report checks rather than violations.

verification.description: How this project renders and re-checks its golden corpus. Needed by the golden A/B, which renders both sides on one machine so platform rasterization differences cancel out.

goldensUpdateCommand.description: argv, not a shell string — a string would need a shell to split it, and a shell is how an argument with a space becomes two arguments.

assets.description: Asset-pipeline facts. Read by the asset adapters.

componentMaturity.description: Where this project's own component-maturity tags live (schema: templates/component-maturity.schema.json). Optional and separate from the suite's internal proven/unverified/experimental/pointer tier — this one is for the project's OWN components (a DsButton, a Table), populated by the project, not by this suite. Absent means no audit can annotate promotion candidates with a maturity tag; it must not be treated as 'everything is stable'.

componentCapabilities.description: Where this project's own component-capabilities manifest lives (schema: templates/component-capabilities.schema.json). Optional, same spirit as componentMaturity: absent means no audit can gate a duplicate-shape match on capability overlap, and that must read as 'no capability signal available', never as 'components have no capabilities' or 'all shape matches are true duplicates'.

verificationGlossary.description: Where this project's own verification-vocabulary glossary lives (schema: templates/verification-glossary.schema.json). Optional: absent means no tooling can resolve what this project's own verification terms (a gate-status word, a tier name, a maturity label distinct from this suite's) mean, and that must read as 'no glossary registered', never as 'this project has no such terms'.

release.description: Config for the release-time checks in bin/ (check_version_consistency.py, deploy_docs_site.py). These compose into a release recipe documented in docs/ADOPTING.md rather than one bundled release.sh — see issue #79's research on why 'deploy' does not generalize past a docs site.

versionSources.description: Files this project considers authoritative for its own version number, read by check_version_consistency.py. Absent or empty means that check has nothing to compare and refuses to run rather than reporting a silent pass.

kind.description: How to pull a version string out of this file. 'jsonKey' needs keyPath; 'regex' needs pattern (first capture group); 'changelogTop' takes the first non-[Unreleased] Keep a Changelog heading.

keyPath.description: Dotted key path into the JSON document, e.g. 'version' or 'packageInfo.version'. Required when kind is 'jsonKey'.

pattern.description: Regex with one capture group matched against the file's text. Required when kind is 'regex' — used for formats this suite has no parser for, e.g. pubspec.yaml's 'version: 1.2.0' line.

docsSite.description: Site-assembly recipe for this project's own docs site, read by deploy_docs_site.py. Absent means that script is a docs-site-only tool with nothing configured, and refuses to run rather than silently doing nothing. No hosting provider is ever hardcoded in the plugin — these commands are this project's own, e.g. rsync, the gh-pages CLI, netlify deploy, or aws s3 sync.

buildCommand.description: argv, not a shell string — a string would need a shell to split it, and a shell is how an argument with a space becomes two arguments.

deployCommand.description: argv, run after buildCommand succeeds. This project's own publish step — this suite supplies no hosting-provider integration.

smokeCheckRoutes.description: Routes to GET after deploy and check the status of. Required and non-empty: a deploy with nothing checked afterward is silently unverifiable.

provenance.description: Per-field provenance (RFC-0002 §3b). Optional and additive: a profile without it keeps working unchanged. It must never be read as 'everything here was approved' — doctor.py reports every field with no entry as UNTRUSTED and prints the ratified-of-total count even when it is 0 of 137, because a provenance block that reports nothing and a profile every field of which was ratified must not look the same.

fields.description: Dotted profile field path (e.g. 'source.root', 'docs.manifest') → how that field got its value. Paths name leaves of this profile; an entry for a path the profile no longer contains is reported, since a ratification of a field nobody has is a ratification of nothing.

quickRef.description: Where this project's optional per-component quick-reference notes overlay lives, read by bin/quick_ref.py alongside componentCapabilities.file and componentMaturity.file when it regenerates docs/COMPONENT-QUICK-REF.md. Free-text and unschemaed on purpose (see quick_ref.py's own docstring): it carries editorial judgement — when to reach for a component, what people get wrong — that neither manifest can derive or verify. Absent means the generated card has no hand-authored blurb, never that the component has none.

_readme: CANONICAL. This is the one definition of a valid .backend-suite/profile.json, and it lives in the plugin because it describes the SUITE's contract, not any one project's. Consumers keep a copy so editors can resolve $schema offline; doctor.py compares that copy against this file and reports drift. Shipped 2026-08-10 after both consumers were found carrying their own editable copies — 341 and 300 lines, structurally identical (48 properties each, zero divergence) but free to diverge with nothing comparing them.
